sources.quote: I think this is really important, but it’s worth distinguishing this from ‘is this research agenda ultimately useful’.

claims.text: Believes research quality and whether a research agenda is ultimately useful are distinct considerations.

sources.quote: This is one of the main reasons that mentorship is so key. I have become a way more effective interpretability researcher by having ready access to Chris to ask for advice, intuitions and direction. And one of my top priorities is absorbing as many of his conceptual frameworks as I can

claims.text: Prioritizes absorbing a mentor’s conceptual frameworks and considers mentorship important to research effectiveness.

sources.quote: Importantly, the goal is not to defer to them, it’s to understand what they believe and why.

claims.text: Prefers understanding what others believe and why over deferring to them.
Enjoys paraphrasing as a way to understand and discuss others’ views.

sources.quote: Don’t just adopt someone’s opinions as your own because they’re charismatic, high status, or well-credentialed. Think about why you think their opinions track the truth better than your own, and in which areas you’re willing to defer to them.

claims.text: Believes deference should depend on why someone’s opinions are likely to track the truth, and should be domain-specific rather than based on status or credentials.

sources.quote: I think some fields score much better on this than others - I’m a lot more comfortable disagreeing with many moral philosophy professors and being a committed consequentialist than I am with eg disagreeing with most algebraic geometers.

claims.text: Is more comfortable disagreeing with moral philosophy professors than algebraic geometers, citing differences in how fields provide feedback about whether one is wrong.
